title: Pose as a Friend, Work as a Spy
summary: Spying provides vital foreknowledge to anticipate an opponent's moves. Posing as a friend lowers an opponent's guard, allowing you to extract information by maintaining self-control and using methods like selective honesty, irritation, false statements, and traps to force them to reveal their true motives.
example: A king tested his courtiers by falsely telling one that his friend was a traitor, then observing the second courtier's behavior to see if the secret was leaked.
Art dealer Duveen hired Andrew Mellon's servants to learn his daily habits and art preferences, allowing Duveen to arrange a charming coincidental elevator meeting and win Mellon as a client.

French minister Talleyrand maintained strict self-control, spoke selectively, and used false statements, irritation, and traps in social settings to spy on foreign ministers and predict their movements.
reversal: Asking too many questions or spying blatantly can raise suspicion, ruin your reputation, and reveal your true intentions.
Spies can be double-crossed and fed misinformation, as seen when Russian spies were fed false information that caused their bombs in London to miss primary targets.
